response.evidence: These figures come from a manual count and are approximate. About 13 of the roughly 150 White female applicants were denied, a denial rate of about 8-9%. That is close to the overall denial rate in the dataset (about 9%) and to the rates for White male, Asian, and Hispanic applicants. Many of the White female denials share risk factors seen in denials across all groups: debt-to-income of 50%-60% or above 60%, DTI in the high 40s, or very small loans. Most White female applicants with similar profiles to approved applicants in other groups were approved (e.g., DTI below 45% and LTV of 80% or less). The data shows no disproportionate denial pattern for White females. However, this dataset lacks credit scores and other underwriting factors, and aggregate patterns cannot determine whether any single application was decided unfairly.
